title: Hosted API location-assurance controls and attestation export workflow
creator: Priya Iyer
description: Background: Customers require deterministic guarantees about where their hosted API requests and derived artifacts are stored and processed. Current residency UI exposes a static country selector but lacks enforcement controls, audit-ready evidence exports, and behavior for failover/soft-fallback cases. Goal: Deliver a location-assurance control surface for Hosted API that: (1) lets tenants declare primary locality preferences and strictness levels (strict, soft-prefer, prefer-with-backup), (2) surfaces expected routing behavior in the Console, (3) records per-request residency trace metadata, and (4) provides an automated attestation export that packages evidence for compliance reviews (request traces, regional routing logs, retention decisions).
acceptance_criteria: Console: New Location Assurance panel on endpoint settings with dropdown for locality mode and single-click 'Generate attestation' action
API: Endpoint config supports 'locality_mode' (strict|soft_prefer|prefer_with_backup) in hosted API management API and is versioned
Routing: Requests carrying tenant locality mode are routed according to documented policy; strict blocks non-compliant region routing and returns a 409 with audit_id fallback for operators
Telemetry: Each request produces a residency_trace_id and a minimal trace JSON persisted to the retention store for the configured retention window
Evidence: 'Generate attestation' bundles a signed ZIP containing routing traces, retention policy snapshot, relevant SLA mapping, and a human-readable summary document
Compatibility: New controls are backward compatible; default mode is 'prefer_with_backup' for existing tenants
QA: Automated integration tests cover strict-mode rejection, soft_prefer degraded routing, and attestation ZIP contents

decisions: Use three-mode locality model (strict, soft_prefer, prefer_with_backup) to balance compliance needs with availability
Attestations will be signed using customer-provisioned KMS when available, else platform KMS with export audit entry
Keep default for existing tenants as prefer_with_backup to avoid breaking traffic
tradeoffs: Strict mode provides strongest guarantee but risks increased request failures and higher latency when preferred region capacity is limited
Soft_prefer keeps availability but requires clear signal in Console and docs that path may traverse other regions
Attestation export provides strong auditability but increases retention footprint and requires retention policy coordination with billing
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Tenant surprises when strict mode causes 5xx or 409 in failover - Mitigation: Add console warnings, enable dry-run mode to surface expected routing before enforcement
Risk: Evidence package may include PII if not filtered - Mitigation: Define redaction rules and minimal trace schema in PRD and legal sign-off
